citations.anchor: queues one delivery per interested endpoint
citations.why: Two matching endpoints produce a single `enqueue` call carrying both rows (queued[0] holds ['a','b']), pinning the "one batched INSERT" clause; the "no network I/O" and "inside the dispatcher's claim transaction" clauses are not asserted by any test.

citations.anchor: the empty set means "everything"
citations.why: An empty eventKinds list admits a kind the endpoint never named and an empty contentTypes list admits an arbitrary type; the workspace clause is pinned only in its real form (allWorkspaces true), since an empty workspaceIds set with allWorkspaces false matches nothing (subscription.ts:69-79).

citations.anchor: routes an entry with no workspace only to an all-workspaces endpoint
citations.why: With one named-workspace and one all-workspaces endpoint, a workspace-less event queues exactly ['all'] — both directions of the rule in one assertion.

citations.anchor: refuses a kind that is not in the catalogue
citations.why: `matches` returns false for a kind with no catalogue descriptor even on an all-workspaces endpoint — the "unknown kind matches nothing" clause.

citations.anchor: subscribes to the catalogue but never to ping
citations.why: Asserts subscriber.kinds contains entry.published and does not contain 'ping' — the "subscriber declares the subscribable set, and ping is not in it" clause.

citations.anchor: queues a fresh delivery keeping the original event id
citations.why: A redelivery through the real API asserts repeat.id !== original.id while repeat.eventId === original.eventId, and that the second request on the wire carries the same eventId with the new delivery id.

citations.anchor: carries a body that names its own delivery and event ids
citations.why: Pins that X-Ortha-Delivery is the row id and X-Ortha-Event-Id is the outbox event id, so the header a receiver deduplicates on is the stable one.

citations.anchor: sends the frozen payload and the attempt number
citations.why: http.send is asserted to receive the claimed row's stored payload verbatim as `body`; a worker that rebuilt the envelope from current state instead of resending what was frozen at fan-out would fail this.

citations.anchor: queues nothing extra when the same event is delivered twice
citations.why: Replaying the outbox row and draining again leaves exactly one webhook_deliveries row — the partial unique index absorbing a redelivered outbox event, proved against a real Postgres.

citations.anchor: queues a fresh delivery keeping the original event id
citations.why: The manual-resend clause: POST .../redeliver succeeds and produces a second row for the same (endpoint, event), so the index does not block a hand-triggered resend.

citations.anchor: never returns the secret again
citations.why: After create, the list body is scanned for the plaintext secret and the single-endpoint body's key set is asserted not to contain `secret` — a leak through either read route fails the test. Routes outside /api/webhooks (e.g. the delivery log) are not scanned.

citations.anchor: rotates the secret and returns the new one once
citations.why: The second of the two permitted routes: POST /:id/secret returns a plaintext secret that differs from the previous one, and the stored hint follows it.

citations.anchor: Webhook endpoints API — the shipped URL policy
citations.why: A second app booted with the shipped policy refuses http://, loopback, RFC 1918, the cloud metadata address and [::1] with 422 at write time — the first of the invariant's two halves. The connect-time half is pinned separately in webhook-http.client.spec.ts.

citations.anchor: refuses a reserved header
citations.why: POST /api/webhooks with headers { 'X-Ortha-Event': … } is a 422 from the server, which is the "enforced on every write, not only in the UI" clause for create; PATCH is not separately exercised.

citations.why: isAllowedCustomHeader — the predicate the endpoints service enforces on write — is asserted to refuse both the X-Ortha- prefix (any case) and the transport headers Host, Content-Length, Content-Type and User-Agent.

citations.anchor: gives up on %i rather than spending five more attempts
citations.why: 400/401/403/404/410/422 all classify as `dead`, pinning "4xx is terminal".

citations.anchor: retries %i — it describes a moment, not the request
citations.why: 408 and 429 classify as `retry`, pinning the two exceptions to the terminal-4xx rule.
5xx classifies as `retry`.

citations.anchor: caps a Retry-After so a receiver cannot park us for a day
citations.why: A 24-hour Retry-After is clamped to MAX_RETRY_AFTER_MS, which is 60 * 60_000 (retry-policy.ts:29) — the "honoured up to one hour" clause.

citations.anchor: treats a transport failure with no status as retryable
citations.why: A response with statusCode null and an error takes markRetrying and never markDead — the "transport failures retry" clause.

citations.anchor: the endpoint changed under the claim
citations.why: Both cases: findForDelivery returning null (deleted) and returning enabled:false assert http.send was never called and the row was closed with markDead — the worker re-reading the endpoint after claiming.

citations.anchor: refuses a contributor, even for reads
citations.why: Contributor — the most privileged non-admin system role (identity/server/src/lib/rbac/system-roles.ts:137) — gets 403 on both GET and POST /api/webhooks, so neither key is held outside admin. The second clause (the editor page requiring webhooks:manage) is unpinned: admin-e2e only asserts the list page's create button is hidden, never that /webhooks/new itself refuses a webhooks:read-only user.

citations.anchor: refuses a host that the URL policy accepts but DNS resolves to loopback
citations.why: The DNS-rebinding half. `localhost` is a name, not an IP literal, so the write-time policy accepts it — the test asserts `assertUrlShape` does not throw on that exact URL first, so the refusal cannot be attributed to the hostname check. The delivery then fails with an error naming the *resolved* address (`resolves to 127.0.0.1`), a message only `assertAddressAllowed` produces, and the loopback receiver records no request at all: the socket was never opened. Deleting `assertAddressAllowed` from the Agent's `lookup` turns this one red (the receiver answers 200) and nothing else.

citations.anchor: delivers to that same host once the deployment allows private networks
citations.why: The paired control for the row above: same URL, same resolver, same client, only `allowPrivateNetworks` flipped — the delivery succeeds with 200 and the receiver records it. So the refusal above is the address policy speaking, not an unreachable name or a broken fixture.

citations.anchor: refuses a private IP literal before it resolves anything
citations.why: The shape check re-run at delivery, not only at save: a literal 127.0.0.1 is refused with the host-naming message (`127.0.0.1 is a private or reserved address`) and explicitly *not* the resolved-address one, which is what keeps the two guards distinguishable in the delivery log. Replacing `assertUrlShape` in `send` with a bare `new URL` fails this test alone.

citations.anchor: reports a redirect as the delivery result instead of following it
citations.why: A receiver answering 302 with a Location on the same host yields statusCode 302 and exactly one recorded request — the second hop is never made. Composing undici's redirect interceptor onto the agent turns it 200 with two requests, so the rule is pinned by outcome rather than by the absence of an option.

citations.anchor: keeps at most responseSnippetBytes of what the receiver sent
citations.why: A 64 KiB answer against a 128-byte cap yields exactly 128 bytes. Unit-level companion to the e2e pin in webhook-delivery.spec.ts; removing either the loop's break or the closing subarray fails it.
